text_input: Patient is a 40-year-old male who presented with a one-week history of repeated episodes of loose stools (six episodes on the day of admission, foul-smelling, watery, black) and one episode of vomiting. He also reported blackish discoloration of the left great toe for two months, previously managed with anticoagulants (Rozela, Ricospirin). Past medical history includes Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (10 years), Ischemic Heart Disease with HFrEF (EF 43%), and Chronic Kidney Disease. Physical examination revealed pallor. Investigations showed anemia (Hb 7.4 g/dL), leukocytosis (WBC 17040 cells/µL), elevated ESR (132 mm/hr), and deranged renal function (Creatinine 3.3 mg/dL, Urea 60 mg/dL). Iron studies showed low TSAT (9.15%) and high Ferritin (753 ng/mL). Diagnosis: Acute gastroenteritis with mild dehydration, IHD with HFrEF, Acute on CKD, left great toe gangrene, T2DM, and anemia of chronic disease. Managed with IV antibiotics (Ofloxacin), insulin, and cardiac medications.
